title: A timing-bound proxy test fails only under concurrent full-suite load, passes in isolation
claim: test/proxy.test.ts's 'a long call's progress is relayed to the client under its own token' asserts a progress notification arrives before a wall-clock deadline; because each such test spawns a real proxy child (npx tsx) and the whole suite runs those children concurrently under node --test, the round-trip can outrun the deadline under load, so the test goes red even though the relay works — and the same test passes every time it is run alone.
appliesTo: This repository's test suite when the full suite runs concurrently (pre-commit, CI, `node --test test/`), on a machine loaded enough that a spawned tsx child + SSE round-trip can exceed the test's wall-clock deadline. Not seen when the test runs in isolation.
expectation: A green test in isolation and a red one in the full run means the code under test is broken and the diff that preceded it caused the failure.
reality: The failure is a load artifact, not a defect: the test waits a fixed wall-clock deadline for a progress notification relayed through a spawned proxy child, and under the concurrent suite the round-trip sometimes lands after the deadline. Re-running the one test alone passes deterministically. A prior session already bumped the deadline 3s -> 8s for exactly this and it can still flake under heavy load.
mechanism: The test spawns a real gateway over stdio (npx tsx) and drives it with raw JSON-RPC, then polls s.notifications until Date.now() passes a fixed deadline. node --test runs the suite's tests concurrently, so dozens of tsx children compete for CPU and the event loop; process startup + the upstream call + the SSE notification relay can then exceed the deadline. Alone there is no contention and it always arrives in time.
workaround: Before treating this test's red as a real regression, re-run it in isolation: `npx tsx --test --test-name-pattern="progress is relayed to the client under its own token" test/proxy.test.ts`. If it passes there, the full-suite failure is load, not your change — do not chase it, and do not weaken the assertion. The durable fix is to wait on the notification event rather than a wall-clock deadline (or raise concurrency isolation for spawning tests), not a bigger timeout.

evidence.command: npx tsx --test --test-name-pattern="a long call's progress is relayed" test/proxy.test.ts
evidence.output:
ok 1 - a long call's progress is relayed to the client under its own token
# pass 1  # fail 0
evidence.note: The same test that reported `not ok 226` under the full pre-commit suite (# pass 396 # fail 1) passes deterministically when run alone.

check.command: node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("test/proxy.test.ts","utf8");const m=/progress is relayed to the client under its own token[\s\S]*?const deadline = Date\.now\(\) \+ \d+000;[\s\S]*?while \(Date\.now\(\) < deadline/.test(s);console.log(m?"wall-clock deadline present (load-sensitive)":"no wall-clock deadline (deterministic wait)");process.exit(m?0:1);'
check.confirmedIf: exit 0, printing 'wall-clock deadline present (load-sensitive)' — the test still gates the relayed notification on a fixed wall-clock deadline, so a concurrent-load run can still flake it.
check.refutedIf: exit 1: the test no longer waits on a wall-clock deadline (rewritten to await the notification deterministically), so the load-sensitive shape is gone.
check.absentWhen: the test is run in isolation, where there is no concurrent load to push the round-trip past the deadline.

observations.note: Hit during pre-commit while committing an unrelated gateway change: the full suite reported `not ok 226 - a long call's progress is relayed to the client under its own token` (# pass 396 # fail 1). Re-running that one test alone passed on the first try. The test already carries an 8s deadline (bumped from 3s in a prior session for this same flake) and still went red under the concurrent suite.

environment.note: Full suite via the pre-commit hook (node --test over test/), which spawns many tsx child gateways concurrently.
